text:
oncall-bot: Paging ash: p99 and streaming-tail stalls detected for hosted API in us-east-1. Alert: SLO breach (p99 > 800ms) and increased streaming stall rate. Automatic paging triggered.
ash (oncall): saw it, joining. any customer-facing pages?
shawn (product-support): one customer reported intermittent streaming stalls causing partial transcripts to drop. CS is triaging.
marta (sre): metrics look like spike in TLS handshakes and retransmits for egress NAT pool in us-east-1c -> host routes showing higher latency. p95 up ~2x, p99 ~3-4x.
kai (infra): checking NAT gateway and conntrack counters. pulling flow logs now.
lee (netops): I see asymmetric egress via nat-pool-5; some instances are flapping to secondary path causing packets to queue. Could be recent route propagation in the VPC.
nash (oncall): running quick checks: `kubectl -n inference exec -it rt-proxy-1 -- netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l` -> high TIME_WAIT count. Also `ss -s` shows backlog.
marta (sre): good signal. streaming stalls often surface from bursty handshake latency. can we confirm handshake RTT to backend inference hosts?
kai (infra): tcpdump on border shows TLS handshake RTTs spiking to 200-400ms for a subset of connections. Also seeing SYN retransmits and occasional RSTs.
lee (netops): traceroute to affected egress IPs shows a hop with >150ms jitter between az-b and az-c. suspect cross-AZ transit in same region hitting a noisy router.
nash (oncall): mitigation proposal: fail traffic away from nat-pool-5 to nat-pool-2 (warm spare), reduce bursting by enabling short-term token bucket on frontend proxies, and temporarily increase streaming stall tolerance for customer-facing routes to avoid cascading errors.
marta (sre): agree. I'll cut a canary to reroute 10% to nat-pool-2 and monitor p95/p99 for 10m. If stable, escalate to 50% then 100%.
kai (infra): switching route target for BGP egress: `aws ec2 replace-managed-prefix-list-entry --prefix-list-id pl-xxxx --remove-entry 10.0.0.0/16 --add-entry 10.1.0.0/16` (simulated). Doing the reroute now to nat-pool-2.
nash (oncall): starting proxy rate-limiter: `curl -X POST https://console/api/proxies/rt-proxy-*/rate_limit -d '{"burst":120,"rate":500}'` (dry-run).
shawn (product-support): informing affected customer that we're mitigating and will follow up. no major data loss reported so far.
marta (sre): canary at 10% in progress — watch logs: `tail -n 200 /var/log/proxy/requests.log | grep "stream-stall"`
kai (infra): BGP change propagated. initial metrics: p99 dropped from ~950ms to ~420ms for the canary subset within 90s.
lee (netops): raw packet captures earlier show ECN markings and retransmit bursts on the bad path. likely queuing on an intermediate router. routing to nat-pool-2 avoids that hop.
nash (oncall): increasing canary to 50% now. watching for regression.
marta (sre): streaming stall rate down 60% in canary. overall p95 trending toward normal. keep an eye on conntrack on nat-pool-2.
kai (infra): conntrack on nat-pool-2 is healthy. we'll drain nat-pool-5: `aws elb deregister-instances-from-load-balancer --instances i-aaaa,i-bbbb` then monitor.
shawn (product-support): notifying customers: "We've routed traffic to a healthy egress path to mitigate streaming interruptions; engineering is monitoring and will provide an update in 30m."
lee (netops): started a ticket with cloud provider for the noisy router in us-east-1 hop 4. provided pcap and timestamps.
marta (sre): after 12m at 50% canary, p99 is stable ~180ms and stall rate back near baseline. proceed to full cutover?
nash (oncall): proceeding to 100% reroute to nat-pool-2 and draining nat-pool-5. triggering runbook step: `incident runbook step: egress-failover -> executed by ash`
kai (infra): 100% moved. draining nat-pool-5. conntrack counts dropping on old pool.
nash (oncall): running post-mitigation checks: synthetic streaming test shows no stalls, p95/p99 within SLO. marking incident as mitigated for now.
marta (sre): assigning postmortem owner: lee. add timeline + root cause: cross-AZ router queuing leading to TLS handshake spikes and retransmits causing streaming tail stalls. Likely intermittent hardware queueing issue.
shawn (product-support): will prepare customer-facing incident note. tagging impacted customers list.
lee (netops): got confirmation from provider that the router had transient firmware-induced queuing; they replaced the unit in the fabric. I'll include their incident id in the PM.
nash (oncall): handing off to marta for postmortem & follow-ups. i'm available if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
marta (sre): thanks — moving to postmortem channel. Logging incident status: mitigation complete, severity: Sev2, start_ts: 2529999999, mitigated_ts: 2530000185.
on-system-note: reactions: :rotating_light: from oncall-bot, :thumbsup: from shawn, :eyes: from kai
